extracted.intended_audience: investigators (PD/PI) applying for or managing NIGMS MIRA (PAR-22-180) grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policy FAQ for preparing, submitting, and managing an NIGMS MIRA (PAR-22-180) application and award, covering eligibility, application content, budgets, review, post-award requirements, and prior approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and distinctive features of MIRA
rubrics_metrics.description: A single NIGMS grant per PI to provide support for NIGMS-related research in an investigator’s lab; distinct features include increased award length, stability, flexibility, and reduced administrative burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI relinquishes other NIGMS support with some exceptions (e.g., resource, training, small business grants). Award levels determined based on the PI's current NIGMS support. MIRA budgets for New Investigators will generally be $275,000 in annual direct costs. Renewals may have flexible funding levels including possible increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of research supported by MIRA (breadth vs narrow projects)
rubrics_metrics.description: The MIRA encompasses the broad program of the investigator's laboratory that is within the mission of NIGMS, in contrast to a narrowly focused project(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MIRA is intended to enable consolidation of NIGMS support for multiple projects that may be disparate; applicants should address rationale for balance of effort and how activities are distinct or complementary. No obligation to develop a single unifying theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on flexibility and impact over specific aims
rubrics_metrics.description: MIRA shifts emphasis away from specific aims and details of proposed experiments and toward the importance of the overall research questions and potential impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review process and criteria emphasize potential impact of the work over details of the approach; applicants should provide high-level narratives focusing on outcomes and impact rather than detailed R01-style aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum required PI research effort (45% rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A PI must devote at least 45 percent of their total research effort to the MIRA (updated per NOT-GM-24-054 effective Oct 1, 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research effort is calculated differently than professional effort (excludes teaching, unrelated administration, clinical duties) and must be expressed in person-months. Examples provided show conversion from percent research effort to calendar months. PIs may request higher effort if well justified. The 45% requirement applies for entire project period including NCEs except in exceptional circumstances with prior approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: How PI effort is verified (Other Support documentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIGMS staff will verify the MIRA research effort requirement using the Other Support documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sum all research effort reported on the Other Support page inclusive of effort to be committed to MIRA; effort on awards whose purpose is education, training, or workforce diversity (e.g., R25s) excluded from calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary charging policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Salary may be charged based on institutional base salary level for up to an amount commensurate with the number of calendar months of effort committed to the MIRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower salary support may be charged; there is no obligatory relationship between percent annual effort and percent annual salary recovered from the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research areas eligible for MIRA
rubrics_metrics.description: Any research area within the mission of NIGMS is eligible for support by a MIRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are strongly encouraged to confer with the program official managing their qualifying award(s) or relevant portfolio before submission; work outside NIGMS mission will be withdrawn prior to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology development allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology development can be included in a MIRA either as the sole focus or integrated with addressing novel biological hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify technology elements as part of overall research program; equipment and data sharing considerations may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical and translational research constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical and translational research within the NIGMS mission may be supported, but with limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanistic clinical trials are permitted when essential to the research program; clinical research involving multi-site recruitment or substantial financial support of multiple collaborators is not allowed; Phase I–III trials designed for safety/efficacy/regulatory approval are not permitted. Pre-application discussion with NIGMS PD is encouraged; adding clinical/translational work after award requires NIH prior approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborators, consortiums and foreign collaborators
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborative research is encouraged, but the MIRA is based on support to an individual investigator's research program; financial support for collaborators is not anticipated in most cases and consortiums are rare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for collaborator support must be extremely well-justified; examples of acceptable cases given (unique resources unavailable elsewhere). Foreign collaborator involvement must be essential, represent unique opportunity, and cannot be supported by the collaborator; consortium agreement may be included rarely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility limits: no overlapping/duplicate applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Flexibility to pursue new directions does NOT allow submission of overlapping or duplicate applications to other NIH ICs, other federal agencies, or private foundations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving funding on overlapping applications could lead to a budget reduction or termination of MIRA. Contact program officer for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicators of change in scope requiring prior approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential indicators of changes in scope include addition or change in approved use of human subjects, vertebrate animals, select agents, or hESCs, or work migrating into another institute's mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These changes require appropriate documentation and prior approval by NIGMS before work is initiated; work that migrates into the mission of another NIH IC would be considered out of scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent submission restrictions to NIGMS
rubrics_metrics.description: On submission of a MIRA application, the PI cannot submit another research grant (R01, R15 or R21) to NIGMS until the MIRA application has been reviewed and a summary statement issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to PAR-22-180 for allowed exceptions. Other types of applications (resource grants, RM1, BTDD, Sepsis R21/R33 phased awards, contracts, training grants, multi-site clinical research, INBRE/COBRE/IDeA-CTR, SBIR/STTR, conference grants) are allowed to be pending concurrently with conditions described in the FAQ (e.g., RM1 participation counts toward 45% effort but no additional funds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed pending applications and special conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain applications may be pending review at the same time as a MIRA (list provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples/conditions: RM1 participation allowable as part of 45% effort but may not receive additional funds; BTDD requires 3 person months toward BTDD and 45% to MIRA; Sepsis R21/R33 phased award R33 issued prior to MIRA may affect New Investigator eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying awards and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A single-PI R01-equivalent award (R01, R35, R37, DP1, DP2, SC1, or NRNM U01) from NIGMS is a qualifying award for a MIRA application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New Investigator eligibility defined (those who have not competed successfully for a substantial, independent NIH research award); ESIs should apply through ESI MIRA NOFO. Multi-PI R01 PIs are not eligible; NIH intramural scientists are not eligible to apply. HHMI and similarly supported investigators are eligible but must carefully explain relationships to other support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time windows for new and renewal submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: New MIRA application: can be submitted any time prior to the original project end date, but no later than the end of the fiscal year following the one in which the qualifying award was set to expire. Renewal MIRA: submit no later than the end of the second fiscal year following the one in which the funded MIRA was originally set to expire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting renewal too early may lead to truncation of current MIRA; consult Key Dates in NOFO (Council Review Date, Earliest Start Date) before deciding when to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on early submissions and start dates
rubrics_metrics.description: NIGMS will not accept applications from MIRA grantees for awards that would begin prior to the end date of the current MIRA except as listed in the NOFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider NOFO exceptions; early submission that would create overlapping start dates may lead to truncation or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether to choose MIRA vs other mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide if consolidation into a single NIGMS program with potential budgetary constraints is worth advantages of MIRA (5 years funding, flexibility, stability, less admin burden).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MIRA renewals generally have higher success rates; unless research program changed significantly, renewing MIRA is often better than switching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application writing approach and high-level narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended approach: explain why the field matters, key questions for next five years, general strategies and alternative approaches, and why you are the right person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep narrative high-level due to limited space; focus on outcomes and impact; do not attempt to pack in all R01-level specifics. Reviewers will evaluate from a broad perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims page policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific aims are not allowed in MIRA applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an institution's submission system forces a specific aims page, enter: 'Per the NOFO instructions, no specific aims are to be submitted.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Current and Pending Support attachment instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information on current and pending research support as instructed in PAR-22-180, which differs from Other Support reported Just-in-Time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish direct costs per year that support research in the investigator's laboratory from support that goes to other investigators. See MIRA webpage for an example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy page limit (6 pages)
rubrics_metrics.description: The research strategy section of a MIRA application is limited to six pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit detail; use biosketch to present needed recent past research contributions; focus on high-level questions and overall program impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing (DMS) plan requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A data management and sharing plan is required in MIRA applications (effective Jan 25, 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include genomic data sharing when applicable. Upload DMS plan in 'Other Plan(s)' attachment field on PHS 398 Research Plan Form. Justify any requested DMS costs in budget justification; if none, state '0'. See NIGMS DMS guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects and delayed-onset studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information form; delayed start and delayed-onset human subjects research are permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delayed-onset studies must be described and prior approval required to add human subjects after award; prior approval requests should include IRB approval and the complete PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix use restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must follow Guide Notice instructions for appendix materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the appendix to circumvent page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional letter of support timing and content (Just-in-Time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional letter of support should be submitted as part of Just-in-Time information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letter must state institution is aware and accepts condition that other NIGMS research awards must be relinquished if MIRA is awarded, and that PI will commit minimum 45% of total research effort to MIRA activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget request philosophy and norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should request budgets similar to their overall NIGMS funding averaged over the past three years; large increases are given only in highly compelling cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On average investigators may get higher budgets through MIRA than NIGMS R01s. For well-funded investigators (> $400k direct costs), a new MIRA may be somewhat lower; 250–400k could be similar/reduced/slightly increased; <250k likely funded at ~$250k unless significant other support; New Investigator MIRA budgets generally ~$275k. Consider case-by-case guidance on renewals (example: request $300k if current $250–275k).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum allowable budget and equipment policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may request no more than $750,000 in direct costs including Equipment per year for a period of 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators are expected to request what is well-justified; equipment can be requested in any year with justification, but MIRA is not intended to fund 'big-ticket' items normally covered by instrument-specific opportunities. New Investigators may request up to $275,000 direct costs excluding equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Itemized budget not accepted; total direct costs required
rubrics_metrics.description: Itemized budget information is not required and will not be accepted; provide a total requested direct cost amount for each budget period (including equipment requests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow SF424 (R&R) Application Guide except as detailed. Complete minimal required R&R fields: select Budget Type, provide period dates; Section A: enter PD/PI with level of effort and enter $0 for Requested Salary and Fringe Benefits; Section C: equipment entries; Section F: add 'Requested Direct Costs' line with total request including DMS costs; leave Sections B, D, E blank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of consortium/subaward costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Consortium/subaward costs are expected to be rare and must be extremely well justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consortium/subaward direct costs (not including consortium F&A) should be included in 'Requested Direct Costs' in Section F. In the Budget Justification provide an estimate of total consortium/subaward costs (direct + F&A) for each budget period, rounded to the nearest $1,000, and list individuals and organizations and whether foreign or domestic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget justification should include specific labeled sections for Data Management and Sharing Costs, Equipment, and Consortium/Contractual Arrangements as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For DMS costs label as 'Data Management and Sharing Justification' and include any requested dollar amount (or '0'). For Equipment include need and equipment quotes. For consortiums list collaborators and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic carryover and use of unobligated balances when ending other grants early
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic carryover authority will apply to MIRA; grants ended early to start a MIRA may initiate the first no-cost extension and retain unobligated balances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds should continue to be expended on aims of active grants that remain in NCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and resubmission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals are allowed for PARs; resubmission (as a revised submission) of a MIRA application is not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not funded, eligible applicants may submit a new application in a subsequent fiscal year; each is considered new, not a resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors in funding decisions and Council involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: NIGMS staff consider study section and advisory council recommendations (scores and summary statement language), Just-in-Time information, and recent grant support history when making funding recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIGMS also considers breadth and diversity of its research portfolio in funding decisions. Summary statements will be made available to the National Advisory General Medical Sciences Council as for other applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific overlap evaluation rule (pre-award)
rubrics_metrics.description: A key test of scientific overlap is whether two grants would both be cited as having supported the same publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIGMS staff evaluate overlap with other active or pending grants prior to making an award and may adjust or terminate MIRA if overlap is determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of MIRA support in publications
rubrics_metrics.description: All research publications supported in whole or in part by NIH must include a specific acknowledgment of NIH grant support with Institute/Center name and specific award number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than one grant supported the research, cite only the grant(s) that supported the research described. Maintain accurate reporting of other support in Just-in-Time and annual progress reports per NOT-OD-19-114.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative supplements eligibility for MIRAs
rubrics_metrics.description: MIRAs will be eligible for certain types of administrative supplements as described in the NOFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check NOFO details for supplement types and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion policy: MIRA cannot be converted to R01
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a MIRA has been issued, that grant cannot be converted to an R01 award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms and conditions continue through project period unless institution relinquishes grant early. At project end, investigator may apply for continuation of MIRA or for a new R01 with requested start date after MIRA project end date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reporting requirements (RPPR) for MIRA
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual reports required using Research Performance Progress Report (RPPR) with additional MIRA-specific instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report any new program directions within NIGMS mission, discuss how work continues to be of high impact, and relationship of any new other support to activities supported by MIRA. These reporting requirements are more specific than for an R01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management of overlap after award
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in other support must be reported in the RPPR; NIGMS will assess whether overlap warrants adjustment to the MIRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain relationship between other support and MIRA activities when reporting; NIGMS may adjust funding level or terms if sufficient overlap exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjusting PI effort and rules on change of PI
rubrics_metrics.description: PI effort on MIRA must remain at least 45% of total research effort for project duration; formal replacement of PI requires prior approval and permanent changes are unlikely to be approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary changes with prior approval may be allowed for sabbatical, medical conditions, disability, or family needs. Standard NIH/NIGMS policies apply for PI inability or absence >3 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling changes to senior/key personnel and grantee organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior/key personnel named in the Notice of Award may be replaced or eliminated only with NIH written prior approval; changes in grantee organization require prior approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard NIH and NIGMS policies apply; consult NIH Grants Policy Statement for details and prior approval procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior approvals required for specific changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard NIH and NIGMS policies govern prior approval events. Examples listed: change in scope (including human subjects, vertebrate animals, select agents, hESCs), additional no-cost extensions beyond first, change in status of PI/senior personnel, change in grantee organization, addition of a foreign component not included in original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addition of animal studies or initiation of delayed-onset animal studies requires notification to NIGMS PO and Grants Management Specialist, IACUC approval, updated VAS, and NIH OLAW written approval before proceeding. Conducting animal research without approvals may result in award reduction, return of funds, and data unusable for the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-cost extension (NCE) special effort rule and exceptional approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: The 45% total research effort requirement applies for the duration of the MIRA, including during a No Cost Extension (NCE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written prior approval for reduction below 45% may be requested for exceptional circumstances during an NCE. Requests should be submitted at least 30 days before effective date and provide evidence of AOR approval; an emailed request must include evidence of AOR approval (cc to AOR is not acceptable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-affected grants and allowed exceptions to relinquishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain types of grants will not be affected by the MIRA and are excluded from the funding level base or from relinquishment requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-affected grants include NIGMS grants that support research resources, training/workforce development/diversity building, clinical trials, SBIR/STTRs, conference grants, cooperative agreements, and portions of multi-component grants that are strictly a core. Also, allowable exceptions to restriction on obtaining other NIGMS funding after MIRA may include funding for clinical trials that are not part of the MIRA investigator's own research program (e.g., serving as site PI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on tR01 and overlap with MIRA
rubrics_metrics.description: An NIH Director’s Transformative Research Award (tR01) assigned to NIGMS would be considered to overlap with a MIRA if the tR01 research falls within NIGMS mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A tR01 that falls in NIGMS mission could not be assigned/awarded by NIGMS while investigator is MIRA-funded; contact PO before submitting a tR01 application.
